name: pySCENIC
method_summary: pySCENIC is a Python implementation of the SCENIC workflow for single-cell gene regulatory network analysis. The selected integration mirrors the pySCENIC GRN step, which infers TF-target adjacencies from a cell-by-gene expression matrix and a predefined transcription-factor list using GRNBoost2 by default or GENIE3 as an alternative tree-based regression method.

threading.upstream_mapping: Wrapper --threads maps to the public pySCENIC GRN runtime control by passing pyscenic grn --num_workers=<threads> with --client_or_address=local. In pySCENIC 0.12.1, find_adjacencies_command() prepares a Dask LocalCluster through _prepare_client(..., num_workers=args.num_workers); that helper uses n_workers=num_workers and threads_per_worker=1. The CLI source pins OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS and MKL_NUM_THREADS to 1, and the wrapper should also avoid exposing worker controls as user params.

required.usage: Required by the selected public entrypoint pyscenic grn as tfs_fname: a TXT file containing one transcription-factor identifier per line. The identifiers must match expression gene ids after any wrapper-internal aliasing.

conditional_required.message: groups is required when execution.mode=group_emulated because ANDREA partitions the dataset by group before running pySCENIC GRN independently per group.
conditional_required.usage: ANDREA uses groups.tsv to create one pySCENIC GRN child run per group; each child receives that group's expression matrix and tf_list, and pySCENIC itself does not consume groups.tsv.

artifacts_aux.description: Combined wrapper and pySCENIC GRN stdout/stderr log.
Raw pySCENIC GRN adjacency table with TF, target and importance columns before conversion to ANDREA network.csv.
Resolved pySCENIC GRN parameters, installation version, execution mode and runtime worker mapping.
Map from any wrapper-internal upstream-safe gene aliases back to exact ANDREA expression gene identifiers.

progress.note: The selected public CLI command logs coarse lifecycle states such as loading expression, inferring regulatory networks and writing results, but it does not expose a stable target-gene or task-partition progress callback through the documented pyscenic grn interface. The wrapper can write coarse progress.json states and preserve upstream diagnostics in pyscenic.log.

method.description: Algorithm passed to pyscenic grn --method. pySCENIC documents grnboost2 as the default GRN reconstruction method and genie3 as the alternative tree-based method.

seed.description: Seed passed to pyscenic grn --seed for regressor random-state initialization. Use null to preserve the upstream default of a random seed by omitting --seed.

oneOf.description: Use null to omit --seed and let pySCENIC choose a random seed.
